found_by: random-policy DRAT and LRAT legs on the 07dccc2 debug binary, 2026-08-11 (jobs 1610523/1610524); ~5% of cases, both proof formats.
diagnosis: AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free in sweep_env_build, on a Ref taken from SweepRound::occ_owned. The faulting access is the 1-byte `k.values[m]` read of a literal decoded out of the bogus record, not the 4-byte `c->garbage()` header read; 9 of the 18 crash bundles in that leg instead abort in clause_at's `ref + CLAUSE_HEADER_WORDS <= arena.size()` assert, which is the same defect caught one step earlier. V5 Sweep's resumable round builds a round-local occurrence index over the arena when Kernel::dense is unusable, which is the standalone/public and random-policy case. A productive seed then commits its consequences inline: sweep_emit_round calls substitute_apply_sweep_equivalences, and do_substitution runs kernel_collect_garbage, which compacts the arena and invalidates every Ref. Kernel::dense IS rebuilt by the collector, so the DefaultPolicy path was unaffected and every tier run was blind; the round-local snapshot was not rebuilt, so the NEXT seed's environment walk dereferenced pre-collection offsets. The read lands wherever the stale offset points, which is why the same defect surfaced three ways -- an ASan report at sweep.cpp, clause_at's header-fits assert (SIGABRT, corpus 015's new failure), and Proof::put_lit's variable-map assert -- and why corpus 004/005 also aborted on that binary. Fixed 2026-08-11: Kernel::arena_generation is bumped by every kernel_collect_garbage; SweepRound stamps its owned snapshot with it and sweep_env_build rebuilds when the counter moved. Checking per seed rather than at the emission site means no future arena-mutating call inside a round can reintroduce the stale traversal, and it costs one comparison when nothing collected. THIS CASE: 07dccc2 aborts within seconds under --random-policy in either proof format (its own repro.sh predicate is kind=crash); the fixed binary reaches a verdict and its model or proof validates.
